title: Find out why the 'encoder cannot match' copy test fails in a busy full test run
goal: A full test run on 2026-11-22 failed once in the cut-export copy tests: a recording the encoder should refuse to copy was copied instead. It passed alone and on the next full run. Find out whether a busy Mac changes the encoder's answer, and make the test steady either way.
notes: Seen in Scripts/test.sh (whole suite) during task music-longer-than-the-edit-stops-where-the-pictu, which touched only sound landing. Output: '✘ Test "A recording the encoder cannot match is left to the ordinary path" recorded an issue at PieceCopyWriterTests.swift:145:15: Expectation failed: an error was expected but none was thrown and "Outcome(copiedFrames: 48, renderedFrames: 0)" was returned' and at :152 the edit.mp4 was left behind. `Scripts/test.sh --filter aRecordingItCannotMatchIsNotCopied` passed (0.27 s), and the next full run passed (1453 tests in 231 suites). Related history: done tasks find-out-why-the-cut-export-test-fails-again-in and the-full-test-suite-stays-green-on-a-busy-mac-wh, and commit ff1766f41 (re-made frames wait for the hardware encoder).
acceptance: The cause is written in this task's log, with the run that shows it
The test passes in five full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row on this Mac
If the copy really can succeed on a busy Mac, the test says what it is checking in a way that holds then

log.note: Cause: under load the hardware H.264 encoder puts extra key frames in unplanned places. Reproduced with /tmp/enc-exp/keys (the test's own clip settings, 320x240 Main, reordering, max key interval 1s): idle runs give keys at frames [0,27,56,83,110,139] or [0,29,58,...]; with 16 parallel 1080p hardware encodes running, the same clip came out with [0,11,40,69,98,125], [0,15,44,73,...], [0,21,31,38,53,63,73,83,104,133], [0,1,11,21,50,...] (60 clips, 27 of them off the idle pattern). The software encoder gives [0,30,60,90,120] every time. The test cut at a fixed 450..<2017ms, which needs frames 13 to 60 (48 frames). When the busy encoder happened to put key frames at 13 and 61, every frame of that piece was a whole group, so the plan copied all 48 and drew none (Outcome 48/0, as in the failing run), the encoder was never asked to match the recording, and nothing was refused. So the copy really does succeed then, correctly: there was nothing to re-encode.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Fix: the test now cuts 50ms after one of the recording's own key frames (read off the file, as 'Cuts on key frames copy every frame' already does), so the frame it opens on always belongs to a group that starts before the cut and has to be made again; the encoder is asked every time, and the 320x240 (level 1.3) recording is refused as the test means. A fixed cut cannot hold on a busy Mac: there the copy genuinely and correctly succeeds with nothing to re-encode. Tests/PhotonzMediaTests/PieceCopyWriterTests.swift only; no app code changed.

Verified: the copy suite passed 3 times in a row with 16 parallel 1080p hardware encodes loading the encoder, then five full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row all exited 0 with the test passing in each (14,872+ tests per run). Run 3 had the helper die on signal 11 in an unrelated test (TestClip.write in SmoothedCopyWriterTests.depth, a real crash, not a half-built .build); the wrapper reran and the rerun passed, the copy test passing in both passes. Filed as the-video-tests-stop-crashing-the-test-run-when. In runs 3 and 5 the whole copy suite finished about 170s late together, which is the suite waiting its turn in a busy run, not this test.

left rough: 'Cuts between key frames keep exactly the frames' and 'stored one way' also expect renderedFrames > 0 at fixed cuts; with four or eight cut points all landing on stray key frames that is far less likely than this test's two, so not changed. If one of them ever fails the same way, give it the same cut-from-the-file treatment.

Cause: a busy hardware encoder adds key frames in unplanned places; when they fell at both ends of the test's fixed cut, every frame was copied and the encoder was never asked, so nothing was refused (reproduced under 16 parallel hardware encodes). The test now cuts just after one of the clip's own key frames so a frame is always re-made. Copy suite green 3x under load, five full Scripts/test.sh runs green in a row. Test-only commit be37fad7c. A separate segfault in the shared test-clip writer seen in run 3 is filed as the-video-tests-stop-crashing-the-test-run-when.
